name: MAX17261METD+
title: 5.1 µA fuel gauge for multi-cell lithium packs, ModelGauge m5 EZ
summary: The MAX17261 is a fuel gauge for a battery pack of one or more series lithium cells: it measures pack current through a low-side sense resistor or a copper trace, the per-cell voltage through an external divider into CELLX, and temperature from its die or an NTC thermistor. The ModelGauge m5 EZ algorithm blends a coulomb counter with a voltage-based model so that most lithium cells need no characterization, and reports state of charge, remaining capacity, time to empty and to full, cycle count and power over I2C. It runs from a 3 V to 5 V supply on BATT, draws 5.1 µA in hibernate, and comes in a 9-bump WLP and a 14-pin TDFN; only the TDFN has the SW pin that switches the divider.

circuits.title: Simple fuel gauge circuit
circuits.description: A stack of series cells feeds SYSPWR; its negative end goes through the protection circuit to the gauge ground and the cell end of RSENSE, whose other end is SYSGND. A 3 V to 5 V regulator off the pack powers BATT, a divider from the pack top to ground gives CELLX its share of the pack voltage, and a 10 kΩ NTC from TH to the cell-side ground senses pack temperature. CSPL, GND and EP meet at one ground point that runs to RSENSE.

circuits.title: Low-side current measurement, removable battery pack
circuits.description: The gauge sits on the system side and meets the pack through three contacts: PACK+, THRM and PACK-. The pack holds the cells, the protection circuit on the negative side and a 10 kΩ NTC from THRM to PACK-. On the system side PACK+ is SYSPWR, a 3 V to 5 V regulator supplies BATT, a divider sets CELLX, and the sense element between PACK- (gauge ground) and SYSGND is a 10 mΩ resistor or a 2 mΩ length of board trace.
notes: The sense element sits close to the CSN and GND pins; the IC corrects for the temperature drift of a copper-trace sense element.

circuits.title: Low-side current measurement, captive battery
circuits.description: A battery built into the product: the cell's positive end is SYSPWR, feeding a 3 V to 5 V regulator for BATT and the CELLX divider; its negative end runs through the protection circuit to the gauge ground at the cell end of a 10 mΩ resistor or 2 mΩ trace, with SYSGND at the other end. No thermistor is fitted on TH.

circuits.title: Multiple-series battery
circuits.description: An N-cell stack. BATT comes from a source follower: Q1's drain on the pack top, its gate held by a 5.6 V zener fed through 500 kΩ, its source on BATT with 2.2 µF. The CELLX divider is (N-1)×500 kΩ plus 300 kΩ above and 200 kΩ below, which puts 40 % of one cell's voltage on CELLX. In the TDFN, Q2 in the upper leg is switched by SW, with 1 MΩ holding its gate low, so the divider conducts only during conversions. A 10 kΩ NTC runs from TH to the cell-side ground.
notes: Without Q2 the divider draws about 8 µA.
Larger divider resistances cost measurement accuracy, smaller ones cost supply current; 200 kΩ is the suggested R1.

operation.text: A coulomb counter is accurate over short spans but drifts as its offset error integrates; a voltage-based estimate does not drift but is limited by how well the cell is modelled. ModelGauge m5 runs both: a voltage fuel gauge estimates open-circuit voltage while current flows, modelling the cell's internal dynamics, and a mixing step weighs it against the counted charge so the voltage result keeps trimming out the counter's drift. It compensates for temperature, load and ageing, forces the error to zero as the cell nears empty, learns capacity over time, and needs no full, empty or rest events to stay corrected.

Most lithium cells run without characterization once three values are written: the label capacity (DesignCap), the empty voltage (VEmpty) and the charge termination current (IChgTerm). ModelID 0 covers most lithium cobalt-oxide cells; ModelID 2 is for NCR/NCA cells and ModelID 6 for LiFePO4, and for both of those a custom characterized model is advised. VChg = 1 selects a charge voltage above 4.25 V (4.3 V to 4.4 V), 0 a 4.2 V charge. Setting Refresh reloads the model, and the IC clears the bit when done.

VE is the loaded voltage at which the gauge reports 0 %, in 10 mV steps over 0 V to 5.11 V, 3.3 V by default. VR is the voltage the cell must recover above before empty detection rearms, in 40 mV steps over 0 V to 5.08 V, 3.88 V by default.

RepSOC and RepCap give state of charge and remaining capacity, held from jumping when the load changes; FullCapRep is updated at the end of each charge. TTE is valid while discharging and TTF while charging; TTF learns the constant-current and constant-voltage phases of earlier charges and assumes later charges look the same. Cycles counts accumulated partial cycles: ten 10 % cycles add up to one. Battery age shows as lost capacity, rising resistance and the cycle count. The register set follows Intel DBPT v2 dynamic power, for estimating the peak power the battery can deliver.

VCell reports 2.5 times the CELLX voltage as a per-cell figure, with AvgVCell its average and MaxMinVolt the extremes since reset. Current is the sense-resistor voltage over ±51.2 mV, factory calibrated, clamped at the register limits; the sense resistance sets both resolution and range. AvgCurrent and MaxMinCurr keep the average and extremes.

Config.TSel = 0 (the default) selects the die sensor, 1 the thermistor on TH, which then also needs ETHRM = 1. For a thermistor reading the IC briefly connects TH to BATT through an internal pull-up, reads TH as a fraction of BATT, then turns the pull-up off to save current; TGain, TOff and Curve convert the ratio to temperature. The die sensor is factory calibrated and ignores those registers. Config.R100 selects a 10 kΩ or 100 kΩ NTC. FTHRM = 1 keeps the bias switch on permanently, which with a 10 kΩ thermistor adds about 200 µA.

With the gauge on the host side, TH also detects the pack: TH rising above VBATT − VDET marks removal and falling back below VBATT − VDET-HYS marks insertion, setting Status.Br or Status.Bi and, with Ber or Bei set, asserting ALRT. With THSH = 1 the IC shuts down when TH stays high longer than ShdnTimer and wakes when a thermistor pulls TH low again.

Writing SHDN = 1 shuts the IC down after the ShdnTimer delay, 45 s by default; for shutdown within 45 s, HibCFG = 0x0000 is written first to put it in active mode. With COMMSH = 1 it also shuts down when SDA and SCL are both held low longer than ShdnTimer, and wakes on a rising edge on the bus. When COMMSH and THSH are both 0, any SDA edge wakes it.

ALRT is open drain and needs an external pull-up. It can fire on battery removal or insertion, on voltage, temperature, current or SOC leaving the window set in VAlrtTh, TAlrtTh, IAlrtTh or SAlrtTh (with Aen = 1), and on each 1 % step of RepSOC (with dSOCen = 1). Write the thresholds before setting Aen. Insertion and removal alerts clear only by clearing the Status bit; threshold alerts clear by software or automatically once back inside the window, as SS, TS, VS and IS choose. Aen gates only the pin; the Status flags still set.

Every IC carries a unique 128-bit serial number. Clearing Config2.AtRateEn and Config2.DPEn makes it appear in place of the dynamic power and AtRate registers at D4h to DFh; setting the two bits again restores those calculations.

The gauge supports sense resistances from 1 mΩ to 1000 mΩ, or a copper trace with temperature compensation. Rechargeable designs pick it from the pack capacity; long-running primary-cell designs generally use a larger value.

BATT needs a supply of 3 V to 5 V, so a pack of several cells needs an external regulator. The CELLX divider is sized to put 40 % of one cell's voltage on the pin. Use 0.1 % resistors. In the TDFN, an N-channel MOSFET driven from SW connects the divider only around each conversion, saving current at the cost of a part.

Take CSN and GND to the sense resistor as Kelvin traces that carry no other current and have no vias, and keep every other ground off them. On the TDFN tie EP directly to GND. Keep the REG capacitor loop small, return it to the GND pin right at the IC, and run a single ground trace from there to the sense resistor. The other pins and their parts have no layout constraints.
